title: Autothrottle Sentry and Variant Phased Cutover for Safe Fallbacks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: During surges and transient infra faults we frequently see noisy 429 spikes and timeout bursts that cause large-scale hard cutovers to lower-capacity model variants. Existing circuit-breaker rules are brittle: they trigger on single-signal thresholds and flip open too aggressively for short lived spikes, causing customer-visible latency and quality regressions.

Goal: Implement an "Autothrottle Sentry" — a multi-signal, probe-driven protective layer that: (1) fuses 429s, timeout rate, p95 latency drift, and per-tenant token error signals; (2) produces a continuous health score with hysteresis and decay; (3) controls graded variant cutovers (phased traffic shifts to fallback variants or regional handoffs) and an adaptive circuit that supports probation periods, rolling reopen, and conservative percent-based throttles.

Scope: Design + implement the scoring function, rule engine, and rollout controller for phased variant cutovers; add telemetry dashboards and a lightweight simulator for empirical tuning. Do not change underlying model binaries or scheduling kernels in this ticket.

Non-Goals: Full tenant billing throttles, long-term capacity planning, or UI polish for rollout controls (console UX will be follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Health score computed from at least four signals (429 rate, timeout rate, p95 latency delta, error-token-rate) and exposed in runtime telemetry
Rule engine supports soft-fallback (shadow/5% traffic), staged cutover (5% -> 25% -> 75%), and hard-fallback paths when health score exceeds severe threshold
Circuit supports open/probation/closed states with configurable decay and minimum-off windows; reopen requires successful pass of probe traffic
End-to-end integration test in staging that simulates a 10-minute 429 spike and demonstrates staged cutover without total failover within 3 minutes
Documentation (runbook + tuning guide) added to Confluence and linked in ticket
Dashboard tile and alerting rule added: health_score > 0.8 for 2m triggers PagerDuty low-severity and creates incident channel

design_notes: Score composition: weighted sum with winsorization. Initial weights: 429_rate(0.35), timeout_rate(0.30), p95_delta(0.20), error_token_rate(0.15)
Hysteresis: need two consecutive 30s windows above threshold to trigger soft-fallback; three consecutive windows to escalate to staged cutover
Decay: exponential decay with half-life of 5 minutes for score components so short microbursts don't permanently bias decisions
Probation: after opening, a minimum-off time of 120s then probe 1% traffic for 30s; require health_score < 0.4 to transition to closed
Staged cutover plan: shadow at 0% (logging) -> mirror 5% -> shift 5% live -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% if metrics are stable at each stage
Safety net: per-tenant emergency lock that prevents cutover beyond configured risk profile (enterprise customers can opt-out), enforced in control plane
Fail-open policy for regions: if global capacity drops < 20% available, prefer regional fallback instead of lower-quality variant to preserve SLAs
tradeoffs_and_risks: More complex scoring increases operational overhead and risk of mis-tuning; mitigate with simulator and staged rollouts
Shadowing and staged cutovers add load to fallback variants — must cap staged traffic to avoid overloading fallback pools
Latency between metric emission and decision may cause lag; tune window sizes conservatively in first rollout
Edge cases: coordinated multi-region degradation may require cross-region orchestration—out of scope for first iteration
implementation_steps: 1) Finalize scoring function and config schema (2 days)
2) Prototype scoring in routing proxy and expose health_score metric (3 days)
3) Build rule engine and staged cutover controller with gRPC hooks (4 days)
4) Add simulator and tuning harness, run golden-path experiments (2 days)
5) Integration tests and staging rollouts behind feature flag (3 days)
6) Documentation and runbook, release notes (1 day)
7) Monitor first-week telemetry and adjust weights/thresholds
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: routing.health_score, routing.component.429_rate, routing.component.timeout_rate, routing.component.p95_delta, routing.component.error_token_rate
Alerts: health_score > 0.65 for 1m -> Ops notify; health_score > 0.8 for 2m -> PagerDuty low
SLO considerations: ensure staged cutovers do not increase 99th latency by >15% for pinned customers
Dashboards: one tile per region + global aggregated health score heatmap
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and decay/hysteresis behaviors
End-to-end staging scenario: inject 429 burst (simulate 20% of requests returning 429 for 6 minutes) and assert staged cutover progression
Chaos run: kill a model pool and ensure controller prefers regional handoff under high-quality-preservation policy
Canary rollout: enable for internal customers, monitor key metrics for 48h before broader rollout
